note: Establish a six-column blend-producing baseline, then use stream compositions and costs to decide where to refine or add heavy-product recovery.
notebook:
PLAN: Start with a six-column direct sequence selling ethane and the C3, C4, C5, C6-paraffin and C6-naphthene blends; assess purity, revenue and cost, then tune weak splits and test adding C7/C8/C9 recovery.
Step 1: baseline direct sequence. Ethane is low value but must be removed for C3 blend purity. C6 paraffins are split from methylcyclopentane/cyclohexane, and the latter from C7+. Moderate stages/reflux avoid overbuilding in the expensive-cost scenario. C7+ remains unsold initially.

note: Replace the ineffective heavy cascade with a direct blend sequence: recover C3 and C4 blends on the light side and C5, C6-paraffin, and C6-naphthene blends on the heavy side.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a six-column blend backbone: C4-/C5+ at feed, then ethane/C3/C4 lights and C5/C6-paraffin/C6-naphthene heavy blends. Step 2 is correcting the root cut and sequence; next tune only impure outlets, then consider C7+ recovery.
The first baseline cut too much C5 into the tops and every outlet was unsellable. Potential blend revenue is large (~$2.35B/yr), so a correct direct sequence should be strongly profitable. C4 and C5 blends avoid difficult isomer separations. The feed column and cold light columns dominate cost, so use moderate stages/reflux and avoid extra heavy columns until blends sell.

note: Use the known convergent R19 backbone and sharpen both heavy blend splits, targeting saleable C5 and C6-paraffin products.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish the convergent R19 backbone, then sharpen the C5/C6+ and C6-paraffin/C7+ cuts to monetize the three large blend streams. Next tune light C3 recovery only if its value exceeds cost, then reduce expensive stages/reflux while retaining 95% purity.
R19 converged and sold C4 blend ($172.5M/yr). Its BT contains all C5 but too much C6, while BBT is only ~80% C6 paraffin. Higher reboil and reflux on B should drive C6 down; a sharper BB cut should exclude naphthenes/C7+. Root cost is high ($158.5M), but potential C5+C6 blend revenue is ~$1.7B/yr. Avoid the failed root at 10% pressure drop; R19 root 50/3/2/0.2 is known to converge.

note: Increase both heavy-column separations sharply: keep nearly all C6 out of the C5 blend and drive naphthenes/C7+ out of the C6-paraffin blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Sharpen the C5/C6+ and C6-paraffin/C7+ cuts on the convergent R19 backbone; then add C3 recovery and reduce costly stages/reflux once blend purities exceed 95%.
R19 sold C4 blend ($172.5M/yr). BT contains all 695 mol/s C5 but 506 mol/s C6 contamination; BBT is only 84% C6 paraffin because the upstream cut sends much C6 to BT. Increase B boil-up to drive C6 downward, and strengthen BB to exclude naphthenes/C7+. R29 showed low B boil-up is ineffective. Potential C5 blend ~$620M/yr and C6-paraffin blend ~$1.1B/yr, so these two cuts dominate economics. Root 50/3/2/0.2 is known convergent.

note: Copy R38's proven light-end recovery and raise the C5/C6 column boil-up moderately to push DMB out of the C5 blend without the excessive C6 carryover seen at boil-up 10.

Its BT is 85% C5 with 10% DMB, so a modest boil-up increase from 3 to 4 should reject most DMB while avoiding the severe C6 carryover seen at boil-up 10. A saleable C5 blend is worth roughly $620M/yr and should make this plant profitable. Root 50/3/2/0.2, T 40/3/2.5/0.1, and TT 30/3/2/0.1 are proven convergent.
